title: HRIRecord
description: Host Response Index record: the aggregation of typed Response results for one (packet, host_class, context) into a floored, fail-closed, matrix-attached score. HRI/1.0 Editor's Draft.

packet_ref.description: Food packet id (FDP FoodPacketID or examples/foods id)

host_class.description: Reference host class, e.g. adult_ir_intermediate. BPS is a function of host class; never omit.

context_ref.description: Optional context (meal timing, prior meal, activity window)

matrix.description: 7 systems x 3 clocks. Systems mirror the engine SevenSystem enum.

critical_staves.description: Cells marked critical for this host_class by the versioned criticality registry.

coverage_tier.description: 0 provisional (input-axis prior only) | 1 modeled (VHM, conformance-green) | 2 measured-acute | 3 measured-longitudinal. Fail-closed: unmeasured critical cells cap the tier.

score_band.description: Floor-aggregated band. Tier 0 may not exceed 'provisional'. Top band requires Tier >= 2 on Energy.acute and Communication.acute.

floor_cell.description: The binding constraint — the cell that set the score. The matrix always ships with the number; this names why.

bounds.description: Uncertainty as first-class: widens with missing tiers and contested evidence.

model_version.description: Required when any cell method = modeled: the VHM version used.

conformance_ref.description: Required when model_version present: CI run id showing the model green on the ward-literature suite. Calibration is a license, not a suggestion.

tempering_alpha.description: Published non-critical uplift constant. v1 proposal 0.25, evidence_state contested; 0 = pure floor.

review_by.description: Nothing persists silently — the anti-1941 field.

class.description: Consumed from the pinned Response spec's classification bounds — BPS never reinterprets raw units.

response_refs.description: ResponseRecord ids with pinned spec versions, e.g. GlycemicResponse/1.0#rec-…

host_conditional_note.description: e.g. 'pass only in deplete hosts — transporter saturation'
